__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Grafana Cloud Prometheus/Mimir data source Alloy's remote_write (config.alloy) is writing into.

title: Telco Churn Serving — Operational Dashboard
description: RED metrics + model/canary health for the deployed serving API. Written by hand (not exported from a live Grafana) as part of docs/PHASE_12A_TODO.md Group 12 — import via Grafana Cloud's dashboard import, mapping DS_PROMETHEUS to the Alloy-fed Prometheus/Mimir data source. Each panel's description carries the alert expression/threshold it's meant to back, per docs/monitoring-metrics.md — Grafana-managed alert rules themselves are created separately (Grafana Cloud console or API), not embedded in this dashboard JSON.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) by (handler). Framework-provided (prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator) — every HTTP call, success or failure. Do not alert on zero traffic alone; a portfolio demo's normal state is near-zero requests — use the scrape-health panel below for "is it down".

panels.title: Request latency p50 / p99
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.50|0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)). Alert: p99 sustained above a chosen SLO (no fixed value shipped here — set empirically once there's real traffic history, same framing as the CPUCreditBalance threshold in docs/monitoring-metrics.md).

panels.title: 5xx error rate
panels.description: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])). Alert: sustained > 0 for a few minutes, or the 5xx/total ratio above a few percent — a working system sits at zero.

panels.title: Predictions by scoring_path
panels.description: sum(rate(predictions_total[5m])) by (scoring_path). champion_only / champion_with_shadow / challenger_canary — a canary configured at fraction=0.1 should show challenger_canary tracking near 10% of total.

panels.title: Predicted probability — p50 / p90 by model_version
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.50|0.90, sum(rate(predicted_probability_bucket[15m])) by (le, model_version)). Not normally a hard alert — investigate-trigger on a shift under a single, unchanged model_version (real drift); a difference between two different version labels is expected, not drift.

panels.title: Model inference time p99 by model
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_inference_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)). A spike here with total request latency (panel 2) flat means the model itself is slow, not a dependency. Also cross-check CPUCreditBalance on a t3.small.

panels.title: SHAP explanation time p99
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(explanation_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)). A sudden whole-distribution shift (not just a longer tail) is the signature of a caching regression — the explainer should be built once per model reload, never per request.

panels.title: Prediction log write failures
panels.description: sum(rate(prediction_log_write_failures_total[15m])) by (route). No healthy non-zero baseline — a sustained rate > 0 for a few minutes IS the alert, no threshold tuning needed. A silent audit-trail gap; the response itself was still served.

panels.title: Customer lookup timeouts
panels.description: sum(rate(customer_lookup_timeouts_total[15m])) by (route). Same framing as prediction_log_write_failures — no healthy baseline, any sustained rate > 0 is the alert. A direct "Postgres is stalled" signal. If both this and panel 8 climb together, suspect a shared Postgres degradation.

panels.title: Champion/challenger agreement rate
panels.description: sum(rate(champion_challenger_agreement_total{outcome="agree"}[15m])) by (mode) / sum(rate(champion_challenger_agreement_total[15m])) by (mode). Not normally a hard alert — disagreement is often the expected, desired outcome of an active evaluation. Read together with panel 11, never alone.

panels.title: Champion/challenger score distance — p50 / p90 by mode
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.50|0.90, sum(rate(champion_challenger_score_distance_bucket[15m])) by (le, mode)). Large distance + high agreement = most customers sit far from the threshold on both sides. Small distance + low agreement = customers cluster right at the threshold.

panels.title: Active threshold (t*) by model_version
panels.description: active_threshold{model_version}. A pure mirror of what the pipeline is actually using to compute served_threshold/decision — plot champion and challenger side by side during a canary. A step here with predicted_probability (panel 5) flat means a policy/threshold change, not drift. Read directly alongside panel 19 (predictions_above_threshold_total's rate) — a policy-change step and a drift-driven step are visually distinguishable that way.

panels.title: Cost scenario constants (base scenario)
panels.description: cost_scenario_constants{constant, model_version} — ltv/cost/retention_rate mirrored unchanged from configs/costs.yaml at model load. Multiply against predictions_above_threshold_total/contact counters at query time for an "estimated campaign spend" view — never a substitute for economics.py's own authoritative, bootstrap-CI'd EV in MLflow.

panels.title: Champion poll health — seconds since last successful poll
panels.description: time() - champion_last_successful_poll_timestamp_seconds. Alert if this exceeds a few multiples of serving.poll_interval_seconds — that specifically means the poll loop itself has stopped running or keeps erroring internally, the exact case the hot-reload's fail-open design is built to hide from everything else.

panels.title: Champion version — registry vs served
panels.description: champion_version_registry vs champion_version_served. Both already read every poll for the version-change comparison the poll loop makes anyway. Alert if they differ for longer than a few poll intervals — catches a reload that's refused (dependency mismatch) or fails outright, which panel 14 alone can't see (the poll tick still completes normally in both cases). A brief mismatch right after a promotion is expected, not an incident.

panels.title: Model reload outcomes
panels.description: sum(rate(model_reload_total[15m])) by (role, outcome). outcome=refused/failed sustained above zero deserves the same "no healthy baseline" treatment as panels 8/9 — these previously only hit logger.warning, never a metric.

panels.title: Contact capacity utilization
panels.description: contact_capacity_utilization — fraction of this cycle's capacity_limit actually filled by contact=true rows, from the most recent /predict/batch call. Not normally an alert target; a sustained 100% says capacity (not the model/threshold) is now the binding constraint, worth a top-K-by-EV policy conversation per ANALYSIS.md.

panels.title: Scrape health — up{job="api"}
panels.description: up{job="api"}. Alert rules (create separately in Grafana Cloud, not embedded in this dashboard): up{job="api"}==0 for 2-3m (Alloy's own scrape-health series — evaluated off-box, so a dead box still triggers it); absent(up{job="api"}) for ~5m, or Grafana's "No data -> Alerting" setting (catches Alloy itself being down or remote_write failing, which up==0 alone can't see since no series would even exist to be 0 — e.g. GRAFANA_API_KEY still REPLACE_ME).

panels.title: Flag rate (predictions_above_threshold_total) by model_version
panels.description: sum(rate(predictions_above_threshold_total[1h])) by (model_version). Mirrors the decision field exactly — served_proba >= served_threshold — not contact (see panel 17 for capacity-constrained contact, a different thing). Read directly alongside panel 12 (active_threshold): this rate can move because the scores moved (gradual, real drift) or because t* itself moved (a step, at the exact moment a new threshold.json loaded) — panel 12 resolves which one directly instead of requiring the inference.
